Posterior distributions of classical stability indices

Source: R/indices.R
bam_indices.Rd

bam_indices() computes five classical stability and superiority indices on every posterior draw of the cell means of a fit, so that each index has a posterior mean, an HPD interval and, for every genotype, a probability of being the best. The indices are those of Wricke (1962), Shukla (1972), Lin and Binns (1988), Annicchiarico (1992) and Eskridge (1990).

Usage

bam_indices(fit, higher_better = TRUE, .prob = 0.25, .alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

fit

a result of bayes_ammi() or bayes_stability().

higher_better

TRUE (default) when larger values of the trait are better.

.prob

error probability \(p\) of Annicchiarico's index (default 0.25).

.alpha

probability \(\alpha\) of the safety-first index (default 0.05).

Value

An object of class c("bam_indices", "bam_result", "list") with

indices

data.table in long form: index, Gen, mean, lower, upper (HPD interval), prob_best (posterior probability that the genotype is the best on this index) and rank_mean (expected rank, 1 = best).

means

data.table: one row per genotype with the posterior means of the indices and the mean of their expected ranks (rank_overall), sorted by it.

Methods: print(), plot(), bam_interpret(), bam_cite().

Details

With \(\eta_{ij}\) the cell mean of genotype \(i\) in environment \(j\) (one posterior draw), \(\bar{\eta}_{i\cdot}\), \(\bar{\eta}_{\cdot j}\) and \(\bar{\eta}_{\cdot\cdot}\) the genotype, environment and overall means, and the interaction \(\epsilon_{ij} = \eta_{ij} - \bar{\eta}_{i\cdot} - \bar{\eta}_{\cdot j} + \bar{\eta}_{\cdot\cdot}\):

wricke

ecovalence \(W_i = \sum_j \epsilon_{ij}^2\); smaller is more stable.

shukla

stability variance \(\sigma^2_i = \frac{G}{(G-2)(E-1)}W_i - \frac{\sum_k W_k}{(G-1)(G-2)(E-1)}\); smaller is more stable.

lin_binns

superiority \(P_i = \sum_j(\eta_{ij} - M_j)^2/(2E)\), \(M_j\) the best cell mean of environment \(j\); smaller is better.

annicchiarico

reliability \(I_i = \bar{Z}_i - z_{1-p}s_{Z_i}\) with \(Z_{ij} = 100\,\eta_{ij}/\bar{\eta}_{\cdot j}\); larger is better (with higher_better = FALSE: \(\bar{Z}_i + z_{1-p}s_{Z_i}\), smaller better).

safety_first

Eskridge's index with the variance across environments, \(\bar{\eta}_{i\cdot} - z_{1-\alpha}s_i\); larger is better (with higher_better = FALSE: \(\bar{\eta}_{i\cdot} + z_{1-\alpha}s_i\), smaller better). bayes_stability() gives the model-based versions of the regression and Shukla models.

Because the indices are computed from the posterior of the cell means, they measure the stability of the expected performance, free of the plot error; the HPD intervals show how well the trial determines them.

References

Wricke, G. (1962). Uber eine Methode zur Erfassung der okologischen Streubreite in Feldversuchen. Zeitschrift fur Pflanzenzuchtung, 47, 92–96.

Shukla, G. K. (1972). Some statistical aspects of partitioning genotype-environmental components of variability. Heredity, 29(2), 237–245. doi:10.1038/hdy.1972.87

Lin, C. S. and Binns, M. R. (1988). A superiority measure of cultivar performance for cultivar x location data. Canadian Journal of Plant Science, 68(1), 193–198. doi:10.4141/cjps88-018

Annicchiarico, P. (1992). Cultivar adaptation and recommendation from alfalfa trials in Northern Italy. Journal of Genetics and Breeding, 46, 269–278.

Eskridge, K. M. (1990). Selection of stable cultivars using a safety-first rule. Crop Science, 30, 369–374.

See also

bam_ammi_indices, bayes_stability, bam_superiority

Other stability: bam_ammi_indices(), bam_stab_priors(), bayes_stability()

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

data(Maiz)
fit <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data   = Maiz
    , .y      = y
    , .gen    = entry
    , .env    = site
    , .rep    = rep
    , .nIter  = 600
    , .k      = 2
    , .burnin = 100
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 1
    , .priors = bam_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .seed   = 1
    , .align  = TRUE
    , .model  = "AMMI"
    , .het    = FALSE
    , .waic   = TRUE
    )
ind <-
  bam_indices(
      fit           = fit
    , higher_better = TRUE
    , .prob         = 0.25
    , .alpha        = 0.05
    )
ind$means
#>       Gen  wricke    shukla lin_binns annicchiarico safety_first rank_overall
